This application coming on for hearing this day, the cou  following:
 ORDER
Applicant has filed this second repeat bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
His earlier application was rejected on merit by this Court vide order date 29.08.2022 passed in MCRC No.36688/2022.

The applicant is in custody since 09.05.2022 in connection with Crime No.19/2022 registered at P.S. STF, Indore, District- Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC.

Brief facts of the case are that complainant Yaduvendra Mishra and Arjun Mishra had filed a complaint with the office of Special Task Force, Indore stating that they had paid certain amount to the applicant and other co-accused persons to get some private job but they did not get the private Narendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69911152/

sentences.text: When they demanded back their money from the applicant and other co-accused, present applicant and other co-accused refused to return their amount.
Accordingly, offence has been registered.
Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
There is no legal evidence available on record to connect the applicant with the aforementioned offence.
After rejection of his earlier bail application, the matter has been amicably settled between both the complainant Yaduvendra Mishra and Arjun Mishra with the applicant.
The applicant has returned the concerned to both the complainants.
Petition under section 320 of Cr.P.C has been filed before the trial Court.
Both the complainants have no objection regarding granting of bail to the present applicant.
Co-accused Sandeep Kushwaha and Devendra Malviya have been enlarged on bail by this Court vide order dated 23.11.2022 passed in MCRC Nos.54694/2022 and 47269/2022 in the similar circumstances.
Therefore, in the changed circumstances, counsel for the applicant has prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

Per-contra, learned counsel for respondent/ State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that earlier bail application of present applicant was rejected on merit by the order of this Court, therefore, applicant does not deserve for bail.

Learned counsel for the complainants submitted that the matter has been amicably settled between both the parties and compromise petition has been filed before the trial Court and both the complainants also filed their affidavits before this Court by stating that they have no objection, if bail is granted to the applicant and also stated that they have received the entire amount, in which the alleged offence has been committed.
Perused the impugned order of the trial Court, the statements of the witnesses as well as the case dairy.
Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties,
nature of allegation as also taking note of the fact that the matter has been amicably settled between both the parties; the amount in question has been returned by the applicant to both the complainants; both the complainants have no objection regarding bail of the applicant; in view of the changed in circumstances, I deem it proper to release the accused/ applicant on bail.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs. 75,000/-
(Rs. Seventy Five Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3) Cr.P.C.

It is made clear that if the applicant is again found to be involved in any other offence during the trial, this order shall stand cancelled automatically without reference to the Court and the police will be at liberty to arrest the applicant in the present case also.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
